title: PET and polyethylene film (multi-agent)
description: Polivac film composed of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) laminated to polyethylene film, used for packaging products
blurb: A laminate of two plastics. Which one gives the essential character?
reference_excerpt: The product in question is Polivac film, which is specifically described as being composed of a layer of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) film laminated to a layer of polyethylene film. The ruling indicates that the PET film constitutes 60 percent by weight and the polyethylene film 40 percent by weight. According to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS), the applicable tariff provision for such products is 3920.62.0000.

text: {"heading":"3920","best_code":"3920.62.00.90","argument":"Heading 3920 covers 'Other plates, sheets, film, foil and strip, of plastics, noncellular and not reinforced, laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials.' The product is a laminated composite film consisting of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) laminated to polyethylene film. The heading text explicitly encompasses laminated plastic films combined with other materials. The product is in film form, used for packaging, and the PET component is the predominant plastic material. Subheading 3920.62 specifically covers PET films, and the 10-digit code 3920.62.00.90 ('Other') is the appropriate classification for PET film laminates not otherwise specified. Chapter 39 note 2 does not exclude this product—it is not a lubricant, wax, chemical compound, or any of the listed excluded articles. The product qualifies as a plastic article under Chapter 39 note 1 (capable of being formed under external influence and retained in shape). Multiple in-force CBP rulings (N338010, N326371) confirm that PET films, including laminated and coated variants, classify under 3920.62.","supporting_rulings":[{"id":"N338010","status":"in_force"},{"id":"N326371","status":"in_force"}],"exclusions_against":[],"strength":0.92}

The heading text explicitly encompasses laminated plastic films combined with other materials. The product is in film form, used for packaging, and the PET component is the predominant plastic material. Subheading 3920.62 specifically covers PET films, and the 10-digit code 3920.62.00.90 ('Other') is the appropriate classification for PET film laminates not otherwise specified. Chapter 39 note 2 does not exclude this product—it is not a lubricant, wax, chemical compound, or any of the listed excluded articles. The product qualifies as a plastic article under Chapter 39 note 1 (capable of being formed under external influence and retained in shape). Multiple in-force CBP rulings (N338010, N326371) confirm that PET films, including laminated and coated variants, classify under 3920.62.

text: {"heading":"3921","best_code":"3921.90.15.00","argument":"Heading 3921 covers 'Other plates, sheets, film, foil and strip, of plastics' and applies to reinforced, laminated, or composite plastic films. The product is a laminated composite of PET (polyethylene terephthalate) and polyethylene film used for packaging. While heading 3920 specifically covers 'noncellular and not reinforced, laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials,' the critical distinction is that 3920 applies when the plastic sheet itself is the primary component combined with other materials. However, when a laminated composite consists entirely of plastic layers (both PET and polyethylene are plastics), and the lamination creates a reinforced or composite structure that gives the material enhanced properties beyond a simple coated sheet, heading 3921 applies as the residual category for 'other' plastic sheets and films. The product's function as a packaging material with barrier and structural properties derived from the laminated composite structure supports classification under 3921 as a reinforced composite plastic film. Code 3921.90.15.00 applies to 'Other' composite plastic products not otherwise specified, with the notation '(229)' indicating products with non-textile reinforcement or composite construction.","supporting_rulings":[{"id":"N357667","status":"in_force"}],"exclusions_against":["Heading 3920 explicitly covers 'noncellular and not reinforced, laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials,' which would apply if the product were a simple laminate of PET to polyethylene without reinforcement. Multiple CROSS rulings (N331595, N338010, N351059, N326371) classify similar PET-based laminated films under heading 3920.62 when the lamination is to polyethylene or involves coating/metallizing of a PET substrate, suggesting 3920 may be the more specific provision for this type of composite."],"strength":0.35}

memo.argument: Heading 3921 covers 'Other plates, sheets, film, foil and strip, of plastics' and applies to reinforced, laminated, or composite plastic films. The product is a laminated composite of PET (polyethylene terephthalate) and polyethylene film used for packaging. While heading 3920 specifically covers 'noncellular and not reinforced, laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials,' the critical distinction is that 3920 applies when the plastic sheet itself is the primary component combined with other materials. However, when a laminated composite consists entirely of plastic layers (both PET and polyethylene are plastics), and the lamination creates a reinforced or composite structure that gives the material enhanced properties beyond a simple coated sheet, heading 3921 applies as the residual category for 'other' plastic sheets and films. The product's function as a packaging material with barrier and structural properties derived from the laminated composite structure supports classification under 3921 as a reinforced composite plastic film. Code 3921.90.15.00 applies to 'Other' composite plastic products not otherwise specified, with the notation '(229)' indicating products with non-textile reinforcement or composite construction.
exclusions_against: Heading 3920 explicitly covers 'noncellular and not reinforced, laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials,' which would apply if the product were a simple laminate of PET to polyethylene without reinforcement. Multiple CROSS rulings (N331595, N338010, N351059, N326371) classify similar PET-based laminated films under heading 3920.62 when the lamination is to polyethylene or involves coating/metallizing of a PET substrate, suggesting 3920 may be the more specific provision for this type of composite.

classification.rationale: Heading 3920 explicitly covers noncellular, non-reinforced plastic film laminated or combined with other materials, which precisely matches this PET-to-polyethylene laminate used for packaging. Chapter 39 Note 1 confirms both PET and polyethylene qualify as 'plastics,' and no chapter exclusion applies. Within 3920, the PET component controls classification to subheading 3920.62 (poly(ethylene terephthalate)), and absent a more specific breakout, the residual 'Other' statistical line 3920.62.00.90 applies, consistent with in-force rulings N338010 and N326371 classifying similar PET laminate films there. The 3921 argument is rejected because that heading is residual for reinforced/composite structures not otherwise provided for, whereas 3920's text directly and more specifically covers this laminated plastic film.
